questions.explanation: SLIC stands for Selective Listing in Combination, a pre-coordinate approach that generates selected combinations of the terms assigned to a document.

questions.stem: What does PRECIS stand for, and who developed it?

options.A: Preserved Context Index System, developed by the British indexer Derek Austin
options.B: Preserved Context Index System, developed by S. R. Ranganathan
options.C: Selective Listing in Combination, developed for the British National Bibliography
options.D: Pre-coordinate Indexing System, developed by the Library of Congress

questions.explanation: PRECIS stands for Preserved Context Index System and was developed by the British indexer Derek Austin for the British National Bibliography.

questions.stem: Why are role operators necessary in a system like PRECIS?

options.A: They indicate the function that each concept plays within a subject statement, such as distinguishing an action from its agent or its object
options.B: They sort every term in the index string into alphabetical order
options.C: They replace the need to identify the individual concepts in the subject
options.D: They allow a searcher to drop the context from an index entry

questions.explanation: Role operators indicate the function each concept plays within a subject statement — for example distinguishing an action from its agent, its object, or another role.

questions.stem: Why is preserving context useful to a searcher?

options.A: It prevents ambiguity by making clear who is using what and what the actual relationships between the concepts are
options.B: It lets the searcher retrieve every document containing any single keyword
options.C: It removes the need to identify the individual concepts of a subject
options.D: It shortens every index string down to one isolated keyword

questions.explanation: A simple unordered list such as students; libraries; databases; use does not make clear who is using what; a syntactic system like PRECIS preserves the relationships between the concepts to prevent this ambiguity.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly describes how a PRECIS-style index string is built?

options.A: Understand the subject, identify the individual concepts, identify the role each concept plays, apply the prescribed role operators, then generate the finished index string
options.B: Apply the role operators first, then identify the concepts, then understand the subject
options.C: List the terms alphabetically, then arrange them by role, then generate the string
options.D: Generate the finished index string first, then identify the individual concepts

questions.explanation: The source gives the practical sequence: understand the subject as a whole, identify the individual concepts, identify the role each concept plays, apply the prescribed role operators, then generate the finished index string from the ordered, labelled concepts.
